To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HIV-1 and simian immunodefivisry (SIV) nucleocapsid protein (NC) display similar NA chaperone activity, HIV-1 NC displays higher DNA compaction energy than SIV NC and HIV-1 NC specifically interacts with SIV Psi RNA, while SIV NC does not interact with HIV- 1 Psi RNA.

HIV-1 NC and SIV NC display only modest differences in their NA chaperone activities, but HIV-1 NC has significantly increased aggregation capability and compaction energy, and SIV NC can cross-species recognize the HIV-1 RNA packaging signal.

(1) the NA chaperone activity and Psi recognition of SIV NC are very similar to those of HIV-1 and (2) SIV NC has a higher propensity to aggregate and is less effective at compacting DNA relative to HIV- 1 NC.
